newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends up on Leslie estimate, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends up on Leslie estimate, technicals.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on bullish input from the Leslie-ADM Elevator survey plus signals the market was oversold and due for a bounce, traders said.

Traders pointed to the sharp drop in December's nine day relative strength index (RSI) late last week which closed at 12.412 Friday as central to the recovery. An RSI of 20 or less is generally considered indicative of an oversold market.
The Dec RSI Monday closed at 23.996, still into oversold territory but active corn harvesting amid near-ideal harvest weather probably will trim rallies, the traders said.
Traders said the corn gains Monday were mainly technical but that the Leslie survey was mildly bullish.

The Leslie-ADM Elevator survey released early Monday pegged 1996 U.S. corn production at 8.906 billion bushels, below the roughly nine billion bushel level predicted recently by several other closely-followed analytical firms.
"The 8.906 was a little below what the trade had expected and maybe was a little supportive," said Mark Cermak, analyst for O'Connor and Co.
Corn futures closed 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 2-1/2 lower, with December up 3-1/4 at $2.92-3/4.
Gains in corn were limited by good harvest weather and forecasts for the mild weather to continue, the traders said.
Slow farmer selling and the overall firm tone in the cash basis market lent support to the market.

Player action central to Monday's corn price trend included Cargill Inc and Continental Grain each buying nearly three million bushels of December, traders said. Cargill Investor Services sold two million December, three million March and one million May, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 48,000 contracts, down from 69,452 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Lee B. Stern and Co bought 800 March $3.00 puts and sold 800 March $3.30 puts at 21 cents and The CHicago Corp bought 400 March $3.00 puts at 13-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, down from 29,564 Friday.
